claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting.
Cloud-provider deletion-protection attributes (such as `deletionProtection`) are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete because of provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while not protected by the provider.

The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection.
Pulumi's `protect` option and resource-level deletion protection are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell the two layers apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` hits a protected resource, the error names the resource URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks cause the cloud API itself to reject delete calls, independent of Pulumi.
Azure Resource Manager returns an error code such as `ScopeLocked` when deleting a resource under a management lock.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to `false` in the program alone is not enough.

Remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection: set the attribute to false in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`.
If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi, `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` `forceDestroy` defaults to `false`, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` `deletionProtectionEnabled` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.

In Azure, `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist; a `CanNotDelete` lock enforced by Azure Resource Manager must be removed before the resource can be deleted.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
